name: Somrai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2025. Palatalization and labialization in the Chadic languages of Chad. Afrika und Uebersee 98: 41-62 (open access, CC BY). https://journals.sub.uni-hamburg.de/hup1/afrikaunduebersee/article/view/392
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Somrai' treats word-level palatalization/labialization prosodies in verbs (data from Deusch 2007 and Roberts 2005/2012); nothing on stress or accent. Valuable for naming the unpublished primary phonology: Deusch 2007 'Soumraye phonology sketch' (SIL Chad Ms.), Roberts 2005 and 2012 Mss.

sources.citation: Schmidt, Sigrid. 2025. Rezension of Adwiraah, Eleonore & Herrmann Jungraithmayr 2021, Orale Literatur in Sibine (Sumray)... / Orale Literatur in Migama (Westafrikanische Studien 43, Koeln: Koeppe). Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. https://doi.org/10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2022_11706
sources.note: Nothing; review confirms the 2021 Koeppe volume (the 'Jungraithmayr 2021' named by the earlier scan) is an interlinear text collection with German translations and indices, no grammar/phonology sketch mentioned.

sources.citation: Miller, Emily Ruthann. 2020. Information structure in Soumraye (Somrai), an Eastern Chadic language. MA thesis, University of North Dakota. xvi+240 pp. https://commons.und.edu/theses/3288/ (PDF fetched sources via Wayback Machine snapshot of the bepress viewcontent URL).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: No word-stress statement; no phonology chapter. p. 96 (sec. 4.1.1): 'Soumraye has three lexical tone[s]: high, mid, and low (Roberts 2012: 4)... also has some grammatical tone in the TAM system... length is contrastive'. 'Stress' appears only for emphatic/focus prominence heard in recordings (pp. 35, 103).

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Herrmann Jungraithmayr. 1982. Le verbe en sibine. In H. Jungraithmayr (ed.), The Chad languages in the Hamitosemitic-Nigritic border area (Papers of the Marburg Symposion, 1979), 192-229. Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 27. Berlin: Reimer. (archive.org item jungraithmayr-ed.-the-chad-languages-in-the-hamitosemitic-nigritic-border-area-1982)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: TOZ GEN AFR. SUDAN C 344; WID Old Widener Afr628.1.5 Bd.27
sources.harvard_location: TOZ GEN AFR. SUDAN C 344; WID Old Widener Afr628.1.5 Bd.27
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Prealable phonologique' (pp. 193-198): syllable structure CV/CVC, consonants (plain/palatalized/labialized), 3 central vowels, and sec. 2.4 'Les tons' (pp. 197-198): three level tones H/M/B plus contour tones BH, HB. Nothing on accent/stress anywhere in the chapter (grep of accent/intensite over the whole chapter: zero hits).

sources.citation: Miller, Emily & Andrea Suter. n.d. (c. 2019-2020). Esquisse grammaticale de la langue chibne [Soumraye]. Ms., SIL Chad.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Full grammar sketch by the current SIL team (cited section-by-section in Miller 2020, incl. sec. 4 on vowel length in verbs); its phonology chapter is the likeliest place for an explicit stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Deusch, Thomas. 2007. Soumraye phonology sketch. N'Djamena: SIL Chad. Ms. (260 verified verbs; cited by Roberts 2025 as the phonological-system sketch of Somrai)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology description of Somrai known; an SIL phonology sketch normally has a suprasegmentals section stating tone and whether stress is contrastive/predictable. Would supersede everything found.

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2012. Phonological structure of Somrai verbs. Paper presented at WOCAL 7, Buea (Cameroon). Ms. (earlier version: Roberts 2005, Phonological structure of Soumraye verbs, SIL Chad Ms.)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Miller 2020 cites its p. 4 for the three-tone system; a verb-phonology paper by Roberts may state syllable prominence/stress alongside tone and prosodies.
